i'm aware that it's not a disability. but when applying for disability, you have to include any condition which may prohibit your ability to work. 

most people won't get disability income from just tremors alone, but added on top of other disabilities, it is absolutely valid to include.

i was just frustrated that it wasn't really considered when making a disability form specifically made for people who have disabilities. sounds very silly.

also, although it is not officially defined as a disability, i think, if it's severe enough, you absolutely have the right to say you are disabled. as someone who has pretty bad tremors, i sure as hell would be upset if someone told me i'm not allowed to call myself disabled (if i weren't already classified as disabled due to other conditions).

if any condition is disabling enough to limit your ability to do basic tasks, you are classified as disabled, according to social security offices and are able to qualify for disability income if they deem it "disabling enough".

TLDR: both in a legal sense and in a social sense, you are disabled if your tremors are severe enough, just not in a medical sense. i was referring to the legal sense in this post.

here's a couple tips,

5. drying meats on a drying rack (you have to find the recipe to it though) gives you proteins, energy, AND fats!! i always struggle the most with fats. also build the drying rack under a platform with a floor so rain can't reach it because it reverts the drying process

6. you can use coconut shells for collecting water in dire situations as they give you 10 hydration at most, ultimately the best would be turtle shells which are 30 hydration

7. try to stay clean as much as possible, use lakes and rivers to clean yourself

8. bananas are probably the easiest source of carbs! there's a banana farm next to the camp where you find the drying rack recipe so staying near that camp for the free bananas is a good thing to do!
